content.title: Sudden cardiac death prevention (excerpt)
content.6.1.1 Secondary prevention of sudden car: Compared with amiodarone, ICDs reduce mortality in survivors of cardiac arrest and in patients with sustained symptomatic ventricular arrhythmias. An ICD is recommended when the intent is to increase survival; the decision should consider the patient's view and quality of life (QOL), the LVEF (survival benefit is uncertain when LVEF >35%) and the absence of other diseases likely to cause death within the following year.
content.6.1.2 Primary prevention of sudden cardi: Analysis of >40,000 patients from 12 pivotal HF trials showed a 44% decrease in rates of sudden cardiac death over ~20 years, likely due to advances in HF therapies. Guideline-recommended therapies (beta-blockers, MRAs, sacubitril/valsartan, CRT pacemakers) reduce sudden-death risk. Amiodarone has not been shown to reduce mortality in HFrEF and, if used, should be with caution. Dronedarone and class I antiarrhythmics (disopyramide, encainide, flecainide) should not be used for arrhythmia prevention due to increased mortality. While ICDs reduce the rate of sudden arrhythmic death in HFrEF, absolute benefit may be lower in well-managed patients; trials such as DANISH showed low sudden-death rates in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) and mixed effects on overall mortality, with subgroup benefit suggested in older patients (≈≥70 years). Two RCTs showed no benefit for ICDs implanted within 40 days after MI; primary-prevention ICDs are contraindicated in that early period. ICD implantation for primary prevention is recommended only if at least 3 months of OMT has failed to increase LVEF to >35%. The cited ICD trials predate routine use of ARNI and SGLT2 inhibitors; whether ICDs reduce mortality in patients with LVEF >35% is unknown. An ongoing trial is examining ICD therapy in patients with scar on CMR and LVEF >35%.
clinical recommendations bullets: Secondary prevention: ICD recommended for survivors of cardiac arrest or sustained symptomatic ventricular arrhythmia when goal is to increase survival, considering patient preference, QOL, LVEF and comorbidities.
Primary prevention: Consider ICD only after ≥3 months of OMT if LVEF remains ≤35% (trials predate ARNI/SGLT2 use).
Avoid class I antiarrhythmics (disopyramide, encainide, flecainide) and dronedarone for prevention due to increased mortality evidence.
Do not implant ICD within 40 days post-MI for primary prevention (no demonstrated benefit).
Recognize that benefit of ICDs may differ between ischaemic heart disease (IHD) and NICM; absolute benefit greater in IHD.
